newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish c.bank caps zloty rise, one-day rates ease.
newsitem.headline: Polish c.bank caps zloty rise, one-day rates ease.

text.p: Poland's central bank rebuked the zloty for rising a notch above the 2.5 percent from parity level with a $10 million intervention only to show the market it was still watching rates carefully, dealers said.

They said the zloty wondered to around 2.51-52 percent from the flotaing parity rate from around 2.44 percent at opening in quiet trade as a result of a change in the dollar/mark rate to which the Polish market did not adjust quickly enough.
"The zloty was slow to follow dollar/mark rate changes, setting off an intervention, but otherwise it was so quiet one could be doing crosswords," said Piotr Czyzewski of ING bank.
The zloty closed at 2.51/2.49 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than the 2.52/2.44 percent close on Wednesday, the last trading day before the long Labour Day weekend.
It closed at 3.1634/39 to the dollar, flat from 3.1610/40 on Wednesday and at 1.8298/01 to the mark, flat from 1.8285/00.
Dealers expected the zloty to stay flat at 2.5 percent from the parity rate tomorrow.
"The NBP showed once again it was committed to keep zloty from firming past the 2.5 percent level," one dealer at a major bank here said.

On the money market one-day rates were flat above the central bank's lombard rate of 25 percent all day, and dealers expected the system to remain tight tomorrow as no net inflows are scheduled for Tuesday.
Overnight rates were stuck at 25.00/26.00 percent while tomorrow/nrext at 24.90/25.60 percent.
"We are likely to keep trading around lombard levels tomorrow as well," said Aleksandra Watroba of Bank Slaski.
